verdicts.quote: Nothing between the socket and :953 compares the index against a bound.
verdicts.why: N01 is the advisory. Same function (sliceMapToSlice, openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:936-962), same source of the number (the bracketed segments of a deepObject query-parameter name, captured by the `\[(.*?)\]` regexp and carried through makeObject/deepSet into buildResObj's array branch), same allocation rule (Atoi each key, take the maximum, grow the slice one element at a time from 0 to that maximum, then a second `make([]any, len(arr))`), and the same missing bound - the quoted sentence says no check exists anywhere between the network and the growth loop, which is precisely the advisory's point that the client's index wins before maxItems is ever consulted. The worked example `?p[arr][2147483647]=x` on a `style: deepObject` parameter whose schema has an array property is the advisory's own reproduction shape, and the impact (single short unauthenticated request, gigabytes, fatal Go OOM that net/http's per-connection recover cannot catch) matches. The reported line :953 is the growth loop rather than the function head the advisory links; that is a line-number difference within the same defect, not a different one. Nearby findings in the batch - N03 (zip decoder buffer/decompression), N08 (nil SchemaRef dereference when `items` is omitted), N02 (double body buffering) - are separate defects in the same file and were not treated as candidates.
